Regluing those two handles gives local data $(g_{\rm loc},n_{\rm loc},d_{\rm loc})=(3-r,r,2)$; the cases are the genus-two one-pair, genus-one two-pair, and planar three-pair slide packets. The handle feet, slide band and small Hamiltonian annuli avoid the bridge disks. Their four interior domain pieces are the same, while only the exterior-face gluing changes. The other meridians are represented by small Hamiltonian translates and the extra marked cut components by split-unlink packets. This graph construction includes separating slides, mixed slides and a dependent bounding pair of nonseparating disks; it does not infer genus two merely from two disk labels. In an auxiliary same-handlebody pair, each $w$ and the $z$ joined to it by that handlebody's ACTUAL bridge arc remain in the same auxiliary face. This does not require an arbitrary old $w,z$ pair to share a face of the original two-ended diagram. Ordinary genus handles and all isotopy/slide supports are disjoint from the marked collars. then $Y\setminus K$ fibers over $S^1$ with fiber $F$.
